statement.essentials: When a pleomorphic adenoma comes back it is harder to treat, and a second recurrence is not rare. Radiotherapy after the repeat operation is linked with fewer further recurrences.
statement.anatomy: Recurrent tumours are often multinodular, MRI is the imaging study of choice, and treatment is individualised; total parotidectomy is appropriate in many patients but may not control the disease.
statement.clinical: In 14 studies of 697 patients with recurrent pleomorphic adenoma, the pooled risk of a further recurrence was 21%: 26% after surgery alone (151 of 538) and 10% with adjuvant radiotherapy (21 of 159).

limitations: The radiotherapy and surgery-only groups were not randomised, so who was chosen for radiotherapy may differ in ways that affect the result, and follow-up times differ. Radiotherapy has its own risks, which the abstract does not address.
